text:
The Bruins were down 4-2 in the third period at TD Garden, and they were not done. Mason Lohrei scored at 13:06, Morgan Geekie tied it with 12 seconds left in regulation, and Elias Lindholm won it 2:32 into overtime, finishing a 5-4 comeback over Chicago. Lindholm, the No. 5 pick in 2013 who last played in Sweden for Brynas before jumping to the NHL, took a pass from Charlie McAvoy and snapped it home from a 27% look, the best chance of the game.

The scoreboard flattered Chicago for most of the night, but the underlying play did not. Our numbers give Boston 3.82 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 3.2, and a 60% chance to win if you replayed every shot, which is what we mean by deserved to win. The third period made the difference: Boston out-chanced Chicago 1.77 to 0.88 in expected goals. Chicago still got a lot out of its best young players. Anton Frondell, the No. 3 pick last June, scored twice on nine shots, and Connor Bedard added a goal and an assist. Arvid Soderblom allowed about 1.2 more goals than his shots deserved, while Michael DiPietro was also below expectation but kept the game close enough.

Boston leaves with a comeback win it needed to earn twice, once in the third and once in overtime. Chicago leaves with a loss after leading by two, and a clear sense that its young scorers did their jobs. We'd watch whether Soderblom steadies himself next time out.
